abstract.text:
This research proposal aims to develop an AANEC-relaxed trapped-surface theorem for spherically symmetric stellar collapse in classical General Relativity. The planned contribution involves replacing pointwise energy conditions with the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC) combined with an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing assumption. This framework will be used to derive a model-dependent compactness threshold for trapped-surface formation via Raychaudhuri-type focusing, subsequently bounding stable non-black-hole remnants through TOV-like stellar-structure assumptions. The study explicitly separates these formal geometric results from astrophysical inferences regarding the observed 2-5 solar mass gap.

The expected outcome of this research is the establishment of a valid proof or counterexample within the declared model class, conditional on the resolution of the proposed averaging assumptions. We anticipate determining whether the combined assumptions of AANEC and explicit averaged focusing suffice to force trapped-surface formation, thereby restricting the viable parameter space for exotic compact objects.

blocks.text: The proposed formal reasoning plan relies on a set of explicitly declared core assumptions. A1 defines the spherically symmetric collapse of massive stars with isotropic pressure. A3 requires the spacetime to be globally hyperbolic and sufficiently regular to support trapped-surface arguments. These definitions constrain the scope of the candidate formalization to classical general relativity under specific geometric and matter-field conditions.

The energy conditions are treated as central hypotheses requiring further mathematical specification. V1 represents the matter field satisfying the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC), which currently requires a precise mathematical formulation within the GR context. Similarly, V2 denotes the independent hypothesis of an explicit averaged null-convergence or focusing condition, which is asserted in the design but lacks a complete mathematical definition at this stage.

Geometric and physical quantities related to the remnant structure are defined for the model class but remain operationally unspecified. V8 represents Misner-Sharp compactness; the operational definition for measuring this quantity in the design context requires human input. V7 refers to the mass of stable non-black-hole remnants, where the unit or domain for measuring stellar remnant mass in this specific formal context is not yet fully defined.

The study identifies independent variables as the satisfaction of spherical symmetry (A1), AANEC (A2), global hyperbolicity (A3), and the explicit averaged null-convergence condition (A4). The final canonical status of this list requires human review to ensure mathematical precision.

Several variables lack precise operational definitions required for rigorous formal reasoning. Specific parameters for EoS (V10), rotation metrics (V11), magnetic field metrics (V12), binary interaction metrics (V13), quantum stress-energy metrics (V14), and supernova explosion energetics (V9) are currently provided. Additionally, the operational definition for measuring compactness (V8) and stellar remnant mass (V7) requires clarification.

The definitions of key geometric objects require formalization to ensure proof validity. V1 (AANEC) is currently user-declared but needs a precise GR formulation. V2 (Averaged Null-Convergence/Focusing Condition) is asserted as independent but lacks the exact mathematical statement intended for the proof. These items are flagged for human input before the formal derivation can proceed to verification.

Evidence Coverage: Registered evidence cards support the proposal's constraints on quantum energy condition violations and the role of supernova explosion physics in determining compact remnant masses. The formal theorem relies on averaged null conditions which are necessary due to pointwise violations, and the application to the stellar mass gap is contextualized by alternative astrophysical mechanisms such as explosion energetics.

Unknown Items: The following premises required for the formal proof remain undefined or unverified and require human input: the precise mathematical definition of assumption A4 (explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition); the specific formulation of assumption A2 (AANEC in the context of general relativistic null generators); and the operational definitions for the independent variables in the formal reasoning plan.

Review Checklist: The following review requirements must be met before finalizing the formal theorem: (1) Define the mathematical structure of assumption A4 to ensure it is independent of AANEC; (2) Specify the form of AANEC required for the Raychaudhuri equation application; (3) Operationalize the 'explicit averaged null-convergence' variable for logical consistency; (4) Operationalize the 'Misner-Sharp compactness' variable for the threshold derivation.

blocks.text: Astrophysical models suggest that binaries with mass ratios similar to GW190814 can form through several channels. The location of the lower edge of the black hole mass gap is dictated by the near-final core mass, which sets the resulting black hole mass. The gravitational-wave phase evolution during the inspiral of binary neutron stars is primarily determined by the chirp mass at low frequencies. These observations provide the empirical context for studying compact object formation.

This proposal plans to derive an AANEC-relaxed trapped surface theorem and stellar mass-gap bound. The work aims to establish formal bounds under specific geometric and matter assumptions, separating the formal result from astrophysical confounders.

The theoretical framework supporting black hole formation relies heavily on Penrose-type singularity theorems, which traditionally require the Null Energy Condition (NEC) to ensure the focusing of null geodesics. However, classical pointwise energy conditions are frequently violated by quantum fields and certain scalar field configurations. To preserve the validity of singularity theorems in semi-classical regimes, the literature has moved toward averaged conditions, specifically the Achronal Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC). The AANEC averages energy density along achronal null geodesics, excluding pathologies associated with closed timelike curves, and is hypothesized to hold even in full quantum gravity.

Observational astrophysics provides critical constraints on these theoretical bounds through the study of compact object populations. A prominent feature in the observed mass distribution of black holes and neutron stars is the lower mass gap in the range of approximately 2 to 5 solar masses. This gap is robust against selection biases and flux-limited detection effects. Theoretical models attribute this discontinuity to the dynamics of core-collapse supernovae, where rapid growth of hydrodynamic instabilities favors either complete envelope ejection or direct collapse, thereby preventing the accumulation of intermediate-mass remnants.

A significant gap remains in the formal verification of trapped-surface theorems under relaxed energy conditions. Current literature identifies a missing 'formal_claim' slot in the evidence plan, indicating a lack of established derivations showing whether AANEC alone, or AANEC combined with an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, is sufficient to force trapped-surface formation in spherical collapse. This unresolved logical connection challenges the proposed mechanism of replacing pointwise NEC/SEC assumptions with AANEC for stellar collapse scenarios.

Furthermore, the identification of a precise boundary variable governing the transition from neutron-star-like remnants to black-hole-like outcomes remains unmapped. While population synthesis studies indicate that theoretical frameworks can produce continuous mass distributions that challenge the sharp discontinuity implied by a hard theorem-based mass gap, a required 'boundary_variable' slot in the relevant evidence cluster for stellar evolution pathways remains uncovered. This highlights the need for further research to constrain the specific physical parameters that dictate remnant type.

2. What quantitative bound on the initial expansion theta_0 is required for the counterexample (CE1) to be invalid? [Needs human input]
3. Are there specific, well-defined numerical solutions (e.g., gravastars) that satisfy all stated assumptions without forming a trapped surface? [Needs human input]

The proposed research aims to develop a formal mathematical framework replacing pointwise energy conditions (NEC/SEC) with the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC) combined with an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition. This work intends to derive trapped-surface thresholds via Raychaudhuri-type focusing and Misner-Sharp compactness, subsequently bounding stable non-black-hole remnants through TOV-like stellar-structure assumptions.

The design assumes that the observed stellar mass gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint rather than a direct theorem-derived prediction, with alternative mechanisms such as supernova explosion physics, fallback, equation-of-state uncertainties, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary interactions serving as confounders.

The audit snapshots show that idea candidates and directions have been available, but they do not provide reliable chronology because temporal order is unknown and iterations are empty. The selected direction, mechanism_replacement, is treated as the proposal baseline.

For planning purposes, the proposal designates mechanism_replacement as the selected research direction. This selection defines the scope of the subsequent formal and empirical work; it is not presented as evidence that this direction is superior or chronologically later.

blocks.text: Assumptions A1-A5 are registered as design premises. Human input is required to resolve A2, A4, and the final canonical field status before formal claims are finalized.

Proposition P1: If spherically symmetric stellar collapse satisfies AANEC, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, then reaching a model-dependent compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation. Proposition P2: Stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale are excluded within this restricted model class.
The central hypothesis P1 posits a formal relation within the specified model class. The final conclusion depends on unresolved assumptions.
- AANEC definition along GR null generators. - Explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition definition. - Final canonical field status.

This research proposal is scoped as a formal mathematical theory design in classical general relativity. The unit of analysis is defined as the formal proof candidate, operating under a theoretical design type rather than an experimental or observational framework.

The core design assumptions for the proposed theorem derivation include:
- Assumption A1: Spherically symmetric collapse of massive stars with isotropic pressure.
- Assumption A2: Matter fields satisfy AANEC along complete null generators, with no uncontrolled quantum ANEC violations.
- Assumption A3: Spacetime is globally hyperbolic and sufficiently regular to support trapped-surface arguments.
- Assumption A4: An explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition holds along the relevant generators as an independent geometric hypothesis.
- V8 Operational Definition: Misner-Sharp compactness is used to evaluate the model-dependent threshold.

The planned method involves replacing pointwise NEC/SEC assumptions with the averaged null energy condition (AANEC), supplemented by the explicit averaged null-convergence assumption. The procedure will derive a trapped-surface threshold via Raychaudhuri-type focusing and Misner-Sharp compactness. Stable non-black-hole remnants will then be bounded using TOV-like stellar-structure assumptions. Throughout this formal process, the observed stellar mass gap is explicitly treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint subject to alternative stellar-physics explanations, rather than as a direct theorem consequence.

The following prerequisites and operational parameters require human input before the formal design can be finalized or executed:
1. Data governance and reproducibility framework definitions must be established.
2. Data management protocols must be specified.
3. Measurement planning details are required.
4. Quality control criteria must be defined.

If the analysis identifies a stable ultra-compact object satisfying the formal assumptions (AANEC, global hyperbolicity, spherical symmetry, regular matter fields, and the A4 averaging condition) yet lacking a trapped surface, the theorem is falsified, requiring restriction or refinement of the averaging condition to preserve validity within the model class. Conversely, if the result favors alternative astrophysical explanations such as explosion energetics, fallback, or equation-of-state uncertainties, the mass-gap inference remains unsupported, necessitating further evaluation of observational discriminators for the stellar mass gap.

sections.title: Expected Outcome Branches and Conditional Conclusions

blocks.text: The proposed formal reasoning relies on specific mathematical assumptions that lack complete definitions. The primary limitation concerns Assumption 4 (A4), where the precise mathematical definition is missing. Consequently, the logical evaluation of counterexamples against this assumption cannot be fully completed. Similarly, Assumption 2 (A2) requires a specific formulation of AANEC in the context of General Relativity null generators to be rigorously evaluated. These gaps prevent the current status from moving beyond a proposal stage.

Human review is required for the following components before further progress can be made:
1. The formal reasoning plan requires qualified human review to validate the logical structure and assumption definitions.
2. Verification of A4's mathematical definition is necessary to determine if the counterexample candidates violate the assumption or satisfy it by default.
3. Clarification of A2's formulation regarding quantum stress-energy and null generators is needed to ensure compatibility with the proposed theorem scope.

Given the absence of verified derivations or rigorous proofs, the hypothesis status remains unverified. The counterexample analysis currently identifies only conceptual models, none of which have been mathematically validated as true theorems or valid counterexamples due to the undefined premises. No experimental or observational results are claimed, as the work is strictly theoretical and limited by the missing definitions.

sections.title: Risks, Limitations, and Human Review Requirements

blocks.text: We formally define the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC), an explicit averaged null-convergence condition along null generators, and the Misner-Sharp compactness for the spherically symmetric model. The precise mathematical formulations are pending human review.

We propose the formal claim that spherically symmetric stellar collapse, under global hyperbolicity and AANEC, forces trapped-surface formation upon reaching a model-dependent compactness threshold. We also propose that stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale are excluded within this restricted model class. The canonical status of these propositions requires human input.

The proof obligations involve verifying the derivation steps from the geometric assumptions to the compactness threshold and its physical implications. The final canonical details of these obligations remain unresolved and require human input.

The proposed forward derivation outlines the logic connecting the initial assumptions to the final conclusion. Step S1 applies the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC) and geometric focusing conditions under the assumption of spherically symmetric collapse and global hyperbolicity. Step S2 defines the Misner-Sharp compactness based on the spherical symmetry assumption. Step S3 identifies a model-dependent compactness threshold derived from the geometric assumptions. Step S4 proposes that if the compactness exceeds this threshold, trapped-surface formation is forced.

The counterexample search plan targets the validity of the proposition that trapped-surface formation is forced under the stated conditions. Candidate CE1 proposes a stable ultra-compact object with compactness just below the threshold, supported by stress-energy satisfying AANEC globally but violating local energy conditions, which fails to form a trapped surface due to large positive initial expansion. Candidate CE2 proposes a semiclassical Einstein equation solution, such as a gravastar or regular black hole, where vacuum polarization creates a stress-energy tensor satisfying AANEC along certain generators but evading trapped-surface formation via local dominance of a large positive cosmological constant in the core.

The reasoning plan currently contains significant gaps and limitations. Rigorous mathematical solutions have not been generated; the candidates are conceptual models derived via LLM proposal. Crucially, Assumption A2 (AANEC) and Assumption A4 (explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition) lack formal mathematical definitions in the current context, which prevents strict logical evaluation of the candidates. Furthermore, the final canonical field status requires human input to resolve these undefined premises and establish a rigorous counterexample search.
